newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Powertech upbeat on real 1997 shr growth.
newsitem.headline: Powertech upbeat on real 1997 shr growth.

text.p: Power Technologies, South Africa's largest power-electrical group, said on Friday it will achieve real earnings growth for shareholders in its new financial year.
"With the divestiture of Gentech, Powertech is now able to focus on its core operations," said Robert Venter, the chief executive officer, in a statement accompanying year end results.
"The group has a satisfactory order book for most of its operations in the year ahead and will continue to build on the successful export performance achieved in the past financial year," he said.

Venter said the firm would continue to benefit from infrastructural development initiatives including electrification, telecommunications and low-cost housing, which should gain momentum ahead of the next election in 1999.
Powertech earlier reported a 50 percent surge in year headline earnings to 56.0 cents a share and the dividend at 18.0 cents from 14.0 before.
Attributable earnings, in part taking account of the disposal of loss-making General Technologies Ltd (Gentech) during the year, rose to 47.2 cents from 36.7 beofre.

Powertech directors said included in the exceptional items charge for the group was a 35.2 million rand loss on discontinuance, which included the operating loss of 25.7 million from March 1 to the closing date of operations.
They said this operating loss had the effect of reducing the selling price during the period of finalising the disposal agreement.

This entire loss was excluded from the calculation of headline earnings as it was considered to be of a capital nature -- which directors said was consistent with the accounting treatment at half year.

Analysts polled by Reuters forecast Powertech's earnings to rise by a consensus 18 percent, although pinning an exact earnings per share figure was problematic as last year's base -- after the Gentech sale -- was unclear.
They expected a dividend of between 15.9 and 17.2 cents with consensus at 16.7.
